# Load packages 
```{r}
# clean slate to be sure
rm(list = ls())

# check for pacman package and install if not found
if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")
  pacman::p_load(tidyverse, here, corrplot, ggcorrplot, heatmap3, patchwork, cowplot, ggpubr, R.matlab, dplyr, BayesFactor,RColorBrewer, psych, ppcor, reshape2, readr) 
  

allsurveys <- read_csv("~/Git/InteroMentalHealth/data/allsurveys.csv")[ ,9:286] #remove  beginning cols for EFA
allsurveys <- allsurveys[, !(names(allsurveys) %in% c("phq_9_10", "phq15_4", "whoqol_4"))] # items with excessive NaNs than usual

# Select the following survey data - Autism, ADHD, Depression, Somatic Symptoms, Stress, Social Anxiety, Trait Anxiety (improves item-subject ratio)
selected_surveys <- allsurveys %>%
  dplyr::select(starts_with("aq10"), starts_with("asrs"), starts_with("mdi"),
                starts_with("phq"), starts_with("pss"), starts_with("sias"),
                starts_with("stai"))

sub_id <- read_tsv('/mnt/raid0/scratch/BIDS/phenotype/demographics/demographics.tsv')$participant_id # participant_id 
selected_surveys <- cbind(sub_id, selected_surveys)

selected_surveys <- na.omit(selected_surveys)

# Load the text details of each item included
surveyitems <- read_csv('~/Git/InteroMentalHealth/data/SurveyItems.csv') #
surveyitems <- surveyitems %>% filter(!Item %in% c("phq_9_10", "phq15_4", "whoqol_4"))# items with excessive NaNs than usual 
prefixes <- paste0("^(", paste(c("aq10", "asrs", "mdi", "phq", "pss", "sias", "stai"), collapse = "|"), ")") 
selected_surveyitems <- surveyitems %>%
  filter(grepl(prefixes, Item)) # Filter the surveyitems based on the prefixes

rm(allsurveys, surveyitems, prefixes) # tidy


# Detect multivariate outliers via Mahalanobis Distance 
distances <- mahalanobis(x = selected_surveys[ ,2:ncol(selected_surveys)], center = colMeans(selected_surveys[ ,2:ncol(selected_surveys)]), cov = cov(selected_surveys[ ,2:ncol(selected_surveys)]))
cutoff <- qchisq(p = 1 - 0.001, df = ncol(selected_surveys[ ,2:ncol(selected_surveys)])) # Cutoff value for ditances from Chi-Sqaure Dist. 
outliers <- distances > cutoff ## Display observation whose distance greater than cutoff value
# Remove outliers from the dataframe
selected_surveys <- selected_surveys[!outliers, ] # 47 multivariate outliers

# save sub_id's 
#write.csv(selected_surveys$sub_id, "~/Git/InteroMentalHealth/data/SubIDs_PsychEFA.csv", row.names = FALSE)
selected_surveys <- selected_surveys[ ,-c(1)]

```

# Network analysis
```{r}
library("bootnet")
library("ggplot2")
library("qgraph")

# Network Estimation: estimate a Gaussian graphical model, using the graphical LASSO in combination with EBIC model selection
# This procedure requires an estimate of the variance-covariance matrix and returns a parsimonious network of partial correlation coefficients.
Network <- estimateNetwork(selected_surveys, default = "EBICglasso")
plot(Network, layout = "spring")

```


```{r}
library(igraph)
#-----------------------------#
##### COMMUNITY DETECTION #####
#-----------------------------#

#spin-glass algorithm for community detection ----#
matrix<- graph.adjacency(Network$graph, mode="upper", diag=FALSE, weighted=TRUE)
set.seed(123)

community_OKI <- spinglass.community(matrix, weights=NULL, vertex=NULL, spins=21, parupdate=FALSE, start.temp=1, stop.temp=0.01, cool.fact=0.99, update.rule="simple", gamma=1, implementation="neg",gamma.minus=1)


#given the presence of negative edges in the glasso, we used the "neg"
#implementation the gamma and gamma.minus were set at 1 to makes existing and
#non-existing links equally important the number of spins was set to 21 (much higher than number of communities detected)

community_OKI
community_OKI$membership
community_OKI$csize

# Create a color palette based on the unique values in the community membership
unique_communities <- unique(community_OKI$membership)

color_palette <- c("khaki1", "lightsalmon", "aquamarine", "mistyrose", "lightblue1", "darkseagreen1", "slategray2", "plum3", "lavender")   
community_colors <- color_palette[match(community_OKI$membership, unique_communities)]


png(filename = "~/Git/InteroMentalHealth/figures/Network/network_plot_rest_communities.png", res = 300, height = 15, width = 20, units = "cm") #
plot(Network, layout = "spring",groups=community_OKI$membership, color = community_colors, posCol= 'brown2', negCol = 'royalblue2')
dev.off()


# Define labels for community detection
names_comm <- c("Self/Social Confidence","Restlessness","Attention Dysregulation","Mentalising","Impulsivity","Depressive Symptoms","Somatic Symptoms","Stress Reactivity","Social Anxiety")
plot(Network, layout = "spring",groups=community_OKI$membership, color = community_colors, posCol= 'brown2', negCol = 'royalblue2')
legend("topright", legend = names_comm, col = color_palette, pch = 16)

```

```{r}
# Community mean scores (reverse-code via a key) 
# selected_surveys: participant x item dataframe (cols = item IDs)

item_names <- names(community_OKI$membership)
if (is.null(item_names)) item_names <- colnames(selected_surveys)
stopifnot(length(item_names) == length(community_OKI$membership))

comm_map <- split(item_names, as.integer(community_OKI$membership))

# items to reverse so higher always = "more of the construct"
reverse_items <- c("aq10_10", "aq10_7", "aq10_2", "aq10_3", "aq10_4", "aq10_8")

# reverse-code (works for 0–3, 1–4, 1–5, etc. by using each item’s observed min/max)
for (it in intersect(reverse_items, colnames(selected_surveys))) {
  x <- selected_surveys[[it]]
  selected_surveys[[it]] <- (min(x, na.rm=TRUE) + max(x, na.rm=TRUE)) - x
}

# participant community averages
community_scores <- as.data.frame(
  sapply(names(comm_map), \(k) rowMeans(selected_surveys[, comm_map[[k]], drop=FALSE], na.rm=TRUE))
)

# rename columns with labels 
colnames(community_scores) <- c(
  "SelfSocial_Confidence","Restlessness","Attention_DysReg","Mentalising",
  "Impulsivity","Depressive_Symptoms","Somatic_Symptoms","Stress_Reactivity","Social_Anxiety"
)

write.csv(community_scores,
          "/figures/Network/community_scores.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)

```



# Read merged data of intero & mental health (& preprocess intero)
```{r}
alldata <- read_csv(here::here("data", "alldata.csv"))
#colSums(!is.na(alldata)) # - 513 HRDT, 267 RRST

# preprocess slope & M-Ratio for intero tasks

# Invert scale of hrd/extero slope (so higher = steeper slope (same as RRST)) (for both intero & extero)
alldata[ ,'HRD_slope'] <- -(alldata[ ,'HRD_slope'])
alldata[ ,'HRDextero_slope'] <- -(alldata[ ,'HRDextero_slope'])


# M-Ratio: Replace negative M-Ratio values with NA 
cols_to_modify <- c("mratio_hrd", "mratio_rrst", "mratio_extero")
alldata[cols_to_modify] <- lapply(alldata[cols_to_modify], function(x) ifelse(x < 0, NA, x))

# M-Ratio: remove high outliers from M-Ratio (MAD-based outlier removal to selected columns) 
alldata[cols_to_modify] <- lapply(alldata[cols_to_modify], function(x) {
  median_x <- median(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  mad_x <- mad(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  x[abs(x - median_x) > 3 * mad_x] <- NA
  return(x) 
})

```

# Correlation matrix & scatterplot functions
```{r}

cormatrix_full <- function(cordata, title, subtitle, savepath) {
  pval_fdr <- psych::corr.test(cordata, method = "spearman", adjust = "fdr")$p 
  rval_fdr <- psych::corr.test(cordata, method = "spearman", adjust = "fdr")$r

  cp1 <- ggcorrplot(rval_fdr,  hc.order=FALSE, p.mat = pval_fdr,
             type='full',  method = "square", insig='blank', sig.level = 0.05,  
             outline.col = "black",
             #lab = TRUE,  # Add correlation values
             #lab_col = "black",               # Label color
             #lab_size = 1.5,                    # Label size
             #digits = 2, # 2 decimal points
             ggtheme = ggplot2::theme_minimal,
             tl.cex = 8,
            colors = c("#4a6fe3", "white", "#d33f6a")) + 
    ggtitle(title) +
    labs(subtitle = subtitle)+
    theme(
      axis.text.x = ggtext::element_markdown(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      axis.text.y = ggtext::element_markdown()
    )
  
  png(filename = savepath, res = 300, units = "cm", width = 15, height = 15) 
  print(cp1)
  dev.off()
}


cormatrix_selected <- function(cordata, xlabel, ylabel, xnum, ynum, savepath) {
  # Correlation plots
  cormatrix <- t(psych::corr.test(cordata, method = "spearman", adjust = "fdr")$r[1:xnum, (xnum+1):(xnum+ynum)]) 
  cor_pvals <- t(psych::corr.test(cordata, method = "spearman", adjust = "fdr")$p[1:xnum, (xnum+1):(xnum+ynum)])
  png(filename = savepath, res = 300, height = ((ynum*3)+2), width = ((xnum*3)+2), units = "cm") # width for factors
  # Plot the correlation matrix with significance markers
  corrplot::corrplot(cormatrix,
                     method = "color",
                     addCoef.col = 'black',
                     cl.pos = 'n',
                     col.lim = c(min(cormatrix), max(cormatrix)),
                     tl.col = "black",
                     col = colorRampPalette(c("#4a6fe3", "white", "#d33f6a"))(100),  #c("blue", "white", "red"))(100)
                     p.mat = cor_pvals,
                     sig.level = 0.05,
                     insig="blank",
                     mar = c(0, 0, 1.75, 0)
                     )$corrPos -> p1
  #text(p1$x, p1$y, round(p1$corr, 2))
  
  # Draw a rectangle around the entire correlation matrix
  rect(0.5, 0.5, ncol(cormatrix) + 0.5, nrow(cormatrix) + 0.5, border = "black", lwd = 2)
  dev.off()
}


# Bayesian corplot: Function to compute a matrix of Bayes Factors for all pairwise correlations
bayes_factor_matrix <- function(data, bayes_factor, savepath) { # , rscale = "medium" - medium is default for width of prior
  # make empty matrix to fill
  bayes_matrix <- matrix(NA, nrow = ncol(data), ncol = ncol(data))
  colnames(bayes_matrix) <- colnames(data)
  rownames(bayes_matrix) <- colnames(data)

  # estimate bayes factors and fill matrix
  for (i in 1:(ncol(data) - 1)) {
    for (j in (i + 1):ncol(data)) {
      
      # first for this correlation data pair remove NAs
      pair_data <- data[, c(i, j)][complete.cases(data[, c(i, j)]), ]
      # estimate bayes factors and fill matrix
      bf <- correlationBF(pair_data[[1]], pair_data[[2]]) #, rscale = rscale
      bf_10 <- extractBF(bf)$bf  # BF10
      if (bayes_factor == 'alternative') {
        bayes_matrix[i, j] <- as.numeric(bf_10)
        bayes_matrix[j, i] <- as.numeric(bf_10) 
      }
      else if (bayes_factor == 'null') {
        bf_01     <- 1 / bf_10 # BF01 
        bayes_matrix[i, j] <- bf_01
        bayes_matrix[j, i] <- bf_01
      }
    }
  }
  diag(bayes_matrix) <- NA # Diagonal is not applicable
  # Mask the lower triangle
  #bayes_matrix[lower.tri(bayes_matrix)] <- NA

  colourpalette <- colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(9, "PuBu"))
  
  cp1 <- ggcorrplot(bayes_matrix, hc.order = FALSE, method = "square", 
  #lab= TRUE, # labels
  #lab_size = 1,
  #digits = 2,
  type = 'lower',
  outline.col = "black",
  ggtheme = ggplot2::theme_minimal,
  tl.cex = 6,
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colors = c("#f3e8ff", colourpalette(100)),
    #colors = colourpalette <- colourpalette(100),
    values = scales::rescale(c(0, 1, max(bayes_matrix, na.rm = TRUE))),
    #limits = c(0, max(bayes_matrix+1, na.rm = TRUE)), 
    name = "Bayes Factor 01",
    na.value = "lightgrey"  # Set a custom color for NA values
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(position='right') +
  theme(
  plot.title = element_blank(),        # Remove the main title
  plot.subtitle = element_blank(),     # Remove subtitle
  axis.title.x = element_blank(),      # Remove x-axis title
  axis.title.y = element_blank(),      # Remove y-axis title
  panel.grid.major = element_blank(),  # Remove major grid lines
  panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),   # Remove minor grid lines
  plot.margin = unit(c(2, 2, 2, 2), "cm"),
  axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = 6), #
  axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6)
  )
  
  png(filename = savepath, res = 300, units = "cm", width = 16, height = 15) 
  print(cp1)
  dev.off()
  #return(bayes_matrix)
}


scatterplot_gg <- function(cdat, yvar, xvar, colour) {
  
  corrdata <- data.frame(apply(cdat, 2, rank))
  pval_fdr <- psych::corr.test(cdat, method = "spearman", adjust = "fdr")$p
  rval_fdr <- psych::corr.test(cdat, method = "spearman", adjust = "fdr")$r

    if (pval_fdr[xvar,yvar] < 0.001) {
      pval = '<.001'
    } else {
      pval = round(pval_fdr[xvar,yvar], 3)
    }
  
  # Remove rows with missing values in xvar or yvar before plotting
  cdat <- cdat[!is.na(cdat[[xvar]]) & !is.na(cdat[[yvar]]), ]

  ggplot(cdat, aes(y= !! sym(yvar), x= !! sym(xvar))) + 
    geom_point(color=colour, alpha=0.5, size = 3) +
    geom_smooth(method=lm , color="#909086", fill="#5d9fcc" , se=TRUE) +
    theme_classic() +
    ggtitle(paste("rs =", round(rval_fdr[xvar,yvar], 3), ", pFDR =", pval))+ 
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 19, face = "bold"), 
          axis.title = element_text(size = 20), 
          axis.text = element_text(size = 20),
          axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 10)), # Add space above x-axis label
          axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 10))  # Add space to the right of y-axis label)
    )
}

# partial correlation function
cormatrix_partial <- function(cordata, covariates, title, subtitle, savepath) {
  # Identify the variables of interest
  vars_of_interest <- setdiff(names(cordata), covariates)
  
  # Initialize matrices for correlations and p-values
  n_vars <- length(vars_of_interest)
  r_matrix <- matrix(NA, n_vars, n_vars, dimnames = list(vars_of_interest, vars_of_interest))
  p_matrix <- matrix(NA, n_vars, n_vars, dimnames = list(vars_of_interest, vars_of_interest))
  
  # Loop through variable pairs to compute pairwise correlations and p-values
  for (i in seq_along(vars_of_interest)) {
    for (j in seq_along(vars_of_interest)) {
      if (i != j) {
        # Subset data for the two variables and covariates
        pair_data <- cordata[, c(vars_of_interest[i], vars_of_interest[j], covariates)]
        pair_data <- pair_data[complete.cases(pair_data), ] # remove missing data for this pair
        
        # Ensure enough rows for computation
        if (nrow(pair_data) > length(covariates) + 2) {
          # Compute partial correlation
          result <- pcor.test(pair_data[ ,vars_of_interest[i]], pair_data[ ,vars_of_interest[j]], pair_data[ ,covariates], method = "spearman")
          r_matrix[i, j] <- result$estimate
          p_matrix[i, j] <- result$p.value
          
        }
      }
    }
  }
  
  # Generate the plot
  cp1 <- ggcorrplot(r_matrix, p.mat = p_matrix, hc.order = FALSE,
                    type = 'lower', insig = 'blank', method = "square", 
                    sig.level = 0.05, outline.col = "black",
                    ggtheme = ggplot2::theme_minimal(),
                    tl.cex = 8,
                    colors = c("#4a6fe3", "white", "#d33f6a")) + #c("#6D9EC1", "white", "#EA5F21FF")) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = n_vars + 0.5, linetype = 3, size = 1) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = 3, size = 1) +
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = 3, size = 1) +
    ggtitle(title) +
    labs(subtitle = subtitle)
  
  # Save the plot
  png(filename = savepath, res = 300, units = "cm", width = 15, height = 15) 
  print(cp1)
  dev.off()
  
  # Return correlation and p-value matrices
  return(list(cor_matrix = r_matrix, p_matrix = p_matrix))
}
```

```{r}
# Joint network: Psychophysics + MAIA + Mental health (EBICglasso)
library(bootnet); library(qgraph); library(dplyr); library(tibble); library(networktools)

# Z-score + estimate GGM
X <- scale(corrdata)
Net <- estimateNetwork(X, default = "EBICglasso", corMethod = "cor_auto") #automatic correlation selection for numerous types of data

# Node blocks (by your column order)
nodes_psy  <- colnames(corrdata)[1:8]   # RRST/HRDT
nodes_maia <- colnames(corrdata)[9:16]  # MAIA
nodes_mh   <- colnames(corrdata)[17:25] # MH domains

grp <- factor(c(rep("Interoceptive Psychophysics (HRDT/RRST)", length(nodes_psy)),
                rep("Interoceptive Sensibility (MAIA)",   length(nodes_maia)),
                rep("Mental Health Symptoms",       length(nodes_mh))))

# Plot
set.seed(123)
qgraph(Net$graph, layout="spring", groups=grp, labels=colnames(corrdata),
       legend=TRUE, posCol="brown2", negCol="royalblue2")


cols <- c("lightskyblue1","lightpink1","khaki1")
node_cols <- cols[as.numeric(grp)]

# shorter labels (example – adapt as you like)
labs <- colnames(corrdata)
labs <- gsub("RRST ", "R.", labs)
labs <- gsub("HRDT", "H.", labs)
labs <- gsub("MAIA", "", labs)
labs[17:25] <- c("Confidence", "Restless", "Inattention", "Mentalising", "Impulsivity", "Depression", "Somatic", "Stress", "Social Anxiety")

png("~/Git/InteroMentalHealth/figures/Network/JointNetwork_Intero_Psych2.png",
    3600, 3000, res=300)
set.seed(123)
qgraph(Net$graph, layout="spring",
       labels = labs,
       color = node_cols,
       posCol="brown2", negCol="royalblue2",
       vsize = 7,          # node size
       label.cex = 1.2)    # <-- label size
legend("topleft", legend=levels(grp), col=cols, pch=16,
       bty="n", cex=1.5)   # <-- legend text size
dev.off()


# --- Direct edges: MH <-> (Psychophysics + MAIA)
A <- Net$graph
edges_mh_psy  <- A[nodes_mh, nodes_psy,  drop=FALSE]
edges_mh_maia <- A[nodes_mh, nodes_maia, drop=FALSE]

edge_tbl <- function(M, from_names, to_names){
  w <- as.vector(M)
  idx <- which(w != 0)
  tibble(
    mh = rep(from_names, times = ncol(M))[idx],
    node = rep(to_names, each  = nrow(M))[idx],
    weight = w[idx],
    abs_weight = abs(w[idx])
  ) %>% arrange(desc(abs_weight))
}

mh_psy_tbl  <- edge_tbl(edges_mh_psy,  nodes_mh, nodes_psy)  %>% mutate(type="MH–Psychophysics")
mh_maia_tbl <- edge_tbl(edges_mh_maia, nodes_mh, nodes_maia) %>% mutate(type="MH–MAIA")

bind_rows(mh_psy_tbl, mh_maia_tbl)

# --- Bridge strength (cross-community connectivity)
b  <- networktools::bridge(A, communities = as.numeric(grp))
bs <- b[["Bridge Strength"]]

tibble(node = c(nodes_psy, nodes_maia),
       bridge_strength = bs[c(nodes_psy, nodes_maia)],
       block = rep(c("Psychophysics","MAIA"), c(length(nodes_psy), length(nodes_maia)))) %>%
  arrange(desc(bridge_strength))


## edge accuracy
library(bootnet)

boot_edges <- bootnet(
  Net,
  nBoots = 1000,
  type = "nonparametric"
)

plot(boot_edges, "edge", plot = "interval")

bt <- boot_edges$bootTable
W <- do.call(rbind, lapply(boot_edges$boots, function(x) x$graph[upper.tri(x$graph)]))

ut <- which(upper.tri(A0), arr.ind = TRUE)
edge_acc <- tibble(
  edge = paste(rownames(A0)[ut[,1]],
               colnames(A0)[ut[,2]],
               sep = " -- "),
  CI.lower = apply(W, 2, quantile, .025, na.rm = TRUE),
  CI.upper = apply(W, 2, quantile, .975, na.rm = TRUE)
) %>%
  mutate(
    ci_width = CI.upper - CI.lower
  )

# identify MH–intero edges
mh_nodes     <- colnames(corrdata)[17:25]
intero_nodes <- colnames(corrdata)[1:16]
edge_names   <- apply(expand.grid(intero_nodes, mh_nodes), 1, paste, collapse=" -- ")




# 3D array of bootstrap adjacency matrices: [node, node, boot]
G  <- simplify2array(lapply(boot_edges$boots, \(x) x$graph))
A0 <- boot_edges$sample$graph

psy  <- 1:8;  maia <- 9:16;  mh <- 17:25

block_sum <- function(r, c, label){
  S <- G[r, c, , drop=FALSE]                 # signed bootstrap edges
  lo <- apply(S, c(1,2), quantile, .025, na.rm=TRUE)
  hi <- apply(S, c(1,2), quantile, .975, na.rm=TRUE)
  tibble(
    type = label,
    n = length(A0[r,c]),
    median_abs_edge = median(abs(A0[r,c]), na.rm=TRUE),
    median_ci_width = median(hi - lo, na.rm=TRUE),
    prop_cross_zero = mean(lo < 0 & hi > 0, na.rm=TRUE)
  )
}

bind_rows(
  block_sum(mh, psy,  "MH–Psychophysics"),
  block_sum(mh, maia, "MH–MAIA")
)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(officer)

r3 <- function(df) mutate(df, across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))

# ---- Table 1: MH–Intero edges (ALL pairs incl. zeros) ----
tab_edges <- bind_rows(
  expand.grid(MH = nodes_mh, Node = nodes_psy, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(Type = "MH–Psychophysics",
           Weight = as.vector(A[nodes_mh, nodes_psy, drop=FALSE])),
  expand.grid(MH = nodes_mh, Node = nodes_maia, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(Type = "MH–MAIA",
           Weight = as.vector(A[nodes_mh, nodes_maia, drop=FALSE]))
) %>%
  dplyr::select(Type, MH, Node, Weight) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(Weight))) %>%
  r3()

# ---- Table 2: Bridge strength (ordered) ----
tab_bridge <- tibble(
  Node = c(nodes_psy, nodes_maia),
  Block = rep(c("Psychophysics","MAIA"),
              c(length(nodes_psy), length(nodes_maia))),
  `Bridge strength` = bs[c(nodes_psy, nodes_maia)]
) %>%
  arrange(desc(`Bridge strength`)) %>%
  r3()

# ---- Table 3: Edge accuracy (ordered by CI width; no crosses_zero) ----
tab_edgeacc <- edge_acc %>%
  transmute(Edge=edge, `CI lower`=CI.lower, `CI upper`=CI.upper, `CI width`=ci_width) %>%
  arrange(desc(`CI width`)) %>%
  r3()

# ---- Table 4: Block bootstrap summary (ordered) ----
tab_block <- bind_rows(
  block_sum(mh, psy,  "MH–Psychophysics"),
  block_sum(mh, maia, "MH–MAIA")
) %>%
  transmute(Contrast=type, `N edges`=n, `Median |edge|`=median_abs_edge,
            `Median CI width`=median_ci_width, `Prop CIs include 0`=prop_cross_zero) %>%
  arrange(desc(`Median |edge|`)) %>%
  r3()

# ---- Table 5: Centrality stability (single row) ----
tab_stab <- tibble(
  Centrality = "Strength",
  `CS coefficient` = as.numeric(corStability(boot_case))
) %>%
  r3()

# ---- write Word document ----
doc <- read_docx()
doc <- body_add_par(doc, "Table 1. MH–Intero edges (including zero edges)", style="heading 2")
doc <- body_add_table(doc, tab_edges, style="table_template")
doc <- body_add_par(doc, "Table 2. Bridge strength (ordered)", style="heading 2")
doc <- body_add_table(doc, tab_bridge, style="table_template")
doc <- body_add_par(doc, "Table 3. Edge accuracy (ordered by CI width)", style="heading 2")
doc <- body_add_table(doc, tab_edgeacc, style="table_template")
doc <- body_add_par(doc, "Table 4. Block bootstrap summary (ordered by median |edge|)", style="heading 2")
doc <- body_add_table(doc, tab_block, style="table_template")
doc <- body_add_par(doc, "Table 5. Centrality stability (case-dropping bootstrap)", style="heading 2")
doc <- body_add_table(doc, tab_stab, style="table_template")

print(doc, target="~/Git/InteroMentalHealth/figures/Network/APA_network_tables.docx")
```
